content: coffee A controlled explosion on a film set near the O2 arena in London ignited a fire that destroyed a van and damaged a car and a lorry. London fire brigade reported that firefighters were dispatched to an open‑air yard on Dock Road in Silvertown just before 8 p.m. on Saturday. The blaze was brought under control after roughly an hour, with twenty‑five firefighters on the scene and no injuries reported. Authorities said the fire followed a pre‑planned filming activity at the site close to the O2 arena, which is slated to host concerts by Niall Horan and Texas next week. The brigade posted on X that the fire at the open air yard in Silvertown is now under control, noting that one van was destroyed and most of a car and lorry were damaged, with no injuries reported. They added that the fire originated from a controlled explosion on the film set that spread beyond expectations, and that crews worked quickly to extinguish it and will remain on site for the rest of the evening. The yard is also near London’s cable car link across the River Thames. A Metropolitan Police spokesperson said they are aware of reports of explosions heard in the area around the O2 in Greenwich.
